elements.texte:
[cheerful] The support team is building an internal tool that lists customers and their email address.

Two customers have no email: on screen, their cell stays empty.

Instead, the tool must show a clear text: “Not provided”.

We start from the customers table, which holds 10 customers.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] That’s the job of coalesce: returning the first value that isn’t null.

Inside the parentheses: the email first, then the fallback text.

The customer Sophie Martin has an email: it shows, and the other value is ignored.

Hugo Laurent’s email is null.

Coalesce so returns the second value: “Not provided”.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Coalesce can take several values:

It goes through them in the given order

And returns the first one that isn’t null.

For Hugo Laurent, the email is null: we move on to the next value.

Hugo Laurent’s phone isn’t null: coalesce so returns his number

And ignores the next value, “Not provided”.

For the tool, which only shows emails, two values are enough.
